scope: P2-7 bounded HTTP business executor, transport isolation and shutdown; no review of own P2-9 implementation
verdict: no unresolved blocker found within reviewed P2-7 scope

runtime_evidence.scope: Linux independent real loopback; copy of root Debug server only; no external endpoints and no ASan claim

static_checks: Business JSON parsing and Service dispatch occur only after bounded admission on business threads; rejected calls never enter Service.
Authentication, route/Host/Origin/content type checks and GET health remain in the IO strand; business RPC wait does not occupy IO.
Admission counts include executing and pending closures, total <= capacity (1..32); stop discards only not-started closures and active completions each decrement once.
Each closure owns Session and request data; business work only posts response construction/write to the captured session strand.
Normal shutdown stops admission and IO, joins request workers while IO and Service still exist, and preserves finite Worker timeout/no-retry semantics.
Startup RequestExecutor thread creation failure calls stop/join; queued tasks are destroyed while IO/Service still live.
limits: Independent runtime probes executed Linux Debug only; no Windows, stress/SLA, TSAN or searchd ASan claim.
Original 64 active-connection limit and five-second socket input/write limits remain; health is not guaranteed under arbitrary connection exhaustion.
An already admitted disconnected request continues its bounded work; it does not release capacity early, cancel automatically or retry.
Existing global JSON synchronization and other application locks are outside this HTTP executor review.
Root full-suite results are separate evidence; this report does not replace exact-final-input full gates or GitHub CI.
